problem:
Let $R=[0,1]\times [0,3]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=8-4x-y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}={0,1},\,{P}_{2}={0,1,2,3},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$

activity_context.topic_title: Approximating Volumes Using Upper Riemann Sums

feedback.problem:
Let $R=[2,5]\times [0,4]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y)=24-2x-3y.$
Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{1}={2,5},\,{P}_{2}={0,1,2,3,4},\,P={P}_{1}\times {P}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the upper Riemann sum $U(f,P).$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's draw the region $R$ and the partition $P.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072318/assets/017b40453041b9485436e21f4966e530b925f6989795283e664692265ca2f814.png)

The upper sum $U(f,P)$ is given by

$$
U(f,P)={M}_{11}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{11})+{M}_{12}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{12})+{M}_{13}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{13})+{M}_{14}\cdot \text{Area}({R}_{14}),
$$

where ${M}_{ij}$ is the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion ${R}_{ij}.$ We pick the *maximum* value of $f$ because we're finding the *upper* sum.

Taking into account the fact that $\text{Area}({R}_{ij})=3$ for all $4$ subregions, the formula for $U(f,P)$ reduces to

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =3\cdot {M}_{11}+3\cdot {M}_{12}+3\cdot {M}_{13}+3\cdot {M}_{14} \\  & =3({M}_{11}+{M}_{12}+{M}_{13}+{M}_{14}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that

- $f(x,y)=24-2x-3y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

- $f(x,y)=24-2x-3y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072318/assets/6ceecc26bb9800a2884202b05144dcecbf988bea7953605e4b33e485a4cb1865.png)

As a result, the *maximum* value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the *smallest* possible $x$ and the *smallest* possible $y.$ This is the value at the *bottom left corner* of each subregion.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14072318/assets/f9ec123fe8048f8463c845527162a3f28ecc3a597f7f57717dde88909f363906.png)

Hence:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{11} & =f(2,0)=20 \\ {M}_{12} & =f(2,1)=17 \\ {M}_{13} & =f(2,2)=14 \\ {M}_{14} & =f(2,3)=11\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}U(f,P) & =3(20+17+14+11) \\  & =186.\end{aligned}
$$
